steps.name: Magna
steps.text: Adele... What a wonderful name. Can I just call you Adele?

steps.name: Magna
steps.text: Have you heard about the thing everyone does the first time they climb a volcano?

steps.name: Magna
steps.text: It's roasting fowlbeast eggs in the lava.

steps.name: Magna
steps.text: But having climbed twenty-seven volcanoes, I can promise you that, when it comes to cooking eggs, lava and Originium stoves make no difference whatsoever.

steps.name: Katia
steps.text: Yeah, you're bound to burn them regardless.

steps.name: Magna
steps.text: Hey! You always eat them right up!

a.text: So this is what a volcano really looks like... It's very from what's in the books.

steps.name: Katia
steps.text: Don't worry, Adele. Just stay right behind me. Anywhere that you see me stepping is going to be safe.

steps.name: Magna
steps.text: If you're nervous, why don't you take my hand?

steps.name: Magna
steps.text: Adele, you asked us before why we love volcanoes, right?

steps.name: Magna
steps.text: I promise you this. Once you see a volcano erupt with your own eyes, you'll never forget the feeling.

steps.name: Magna
steps.text: I like to sit on the slopes and meditate. The land and us are both full of mystery, and even if we spend our lifetimes seeking answers, we may not be able to solve even a tiny fraction of them. Still, I do enjoy the puzzle solving.

steps.name: Katia
steps.text: Mankind may have invented nomadic cities, but we still haven't completely figured out how Catastrophes form. We may have invented many tools with Originium, but we also have no way to counter their effects when they backfire.

steps.name: Katia
steps.text: Humans need to admit just how insignificant they are when they come face to face with nature's mighty forces. That way, they won't spend so much energy meaninglessly slaughtering each other.

steps.name: Magna
steps.text: Adele, don't mind Katia's pessimism. Not everywhere is as simple as Siesta.

steps.name: Magna
steps.text: It's natural for him to grumble when, as a scholar, he's all wrapped up in noble bickering, but on these issues, I've always looked at things quite differently from him.

steps.name: Magna
steps.text: Naturally, humans are insignificant, but it's exactly because we are so insignificant that we can live on the land.

a.text: Life is insignificant, yet mankind insists on seeking answers in the earth with their insignificant lives. When you look at it that way, when they are inevitably swallowed by up by that same earth, you can only accept their fate as par for the course.
But how am I supposed to face the abyss alone after the two of you are gone?

steps.name: Worker
steps.text: Professor Keller, here's the last two hours of data we got from Monitoring Station No. 1 before the signal was lost.

steps.name: Worker
steps.text: We've never seen abnormalities like this... We have no choice but to consult you...

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: The surface gas concentration hasn't changed. How did the temperature go up by this much so quickly?

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: If the data were real, then that means the energy accumulated in Mount Siesta suddenly increased tenfold... No, it's not possible, no matter how you slice it.

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: Ignore it as a point anomaly.

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: Inform the city government that the volcano has become more active and to have the citizens prepare. That's all we can do.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Professor, this may not be your usual point anomaly.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: My parents mentioned similar situations in their research notes... The temperatures in the volcano's surroundings were abnormally high and didn't match the other data.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: They never found the cause, but this can't just be explained as a coincidence.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Professor, shouldn't we head there to take a look at the situation ourselves?

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: Monitoring Station No. 1 is about midway up the volcano. It's very dangerous to go up there now.

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: This kind of data anomaly could just be an equipment malfunction. There's no need to take the risk and head there for on-site inspections. We can adjust the final observation results based on the other monitoring stations' data later.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Professor Keller, I don't understand...

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: You kept saying how important this observation was going to be, that it's an opportunity that many scholars had been waiting for. Tens of thousands of the residents could have their lives upended. Shouldn't we be as careful about this as we possibly can?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: If we run away now... isn't that admitting their sacrifice was for nothing?
The girl's voice is quiet, and her body is trembling ever so slightly. It seems that she spent quite a bit of her strength just to express her honest opinion.
Keller appears a little dazed.

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: Right...

a.text: How could a sacrifice like that be meaningful?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: It doesn't look like I'm going to convince you...

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: If you aren't willing to go, is it okay if I go alone...?

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: Don't be absurd. We don't know what's going on at the volcano. I can't let you go somewhere so dangerous all by yourself—

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Professor Keller... Would you return my mother's protective suit to me?

steps.name: Passerby A
steps.text: Is there anything we can do but eat? If this goes on, my stomach's gonna explode...

steps.name: Passerby B
steps.text: Listen to a few more guitar songs?

steps.name: Passerby A
steps.text: Hm... I kinda feel there's meant to be something more exciting...

steps.name: Passerby B
steps.text: How is this supposed to be as exciting as the Obsidian Festival? The crowds were massive, the streets and shops were endless, and the music never ever stopped. That was so much better!

steps.name: Cold Drinks Shop Owner
steps.text: Say what you will, but this party reminds me of the first Obsidian Festival.

steps.name: Passerby B
steps.text: The first one? How many years ago was that?

steps.name: Cold Drinks Shop Owner
steps.text: Not a whole lot of people still remember, but the first festival was actually held in the mines. It was run but a bunch of miners.

steps.name: Cold Drinks Shop Owner
steps.text: Yeah, there weren't that many people, much less decent musicians. They just strummed their guitars and played a few songs they wrote. That's how it all began...

steps.name: Cold Drinks Shop Owner
steps.text: Nobody back then could've imagined it would grow so big and attract so many guests.

steps.name: Passerby A
steps.text: Is the after party gonna come back, too?

steps.name: Cold Drinks Shop Owner
steps.text: Hahaha, now no one can say for sure!

steps.name: Passerby B
steps.text: But if you guys are moving to the city center, does that mean these shops are gonna be closed forever?

steps.name: Male Instrument Shop Owner
steps.text: Probably. We might have to make a living some other way, but nobody lives a life without change.

steps.name: Male Instrument Shop Owner
steps.text: That said, whenever we have free time, we might come here and set up a stall, play a few songs. If anybody comes, we'll give them a few skewers to snack on. If nobody comes, we'll just look at the sea, at what lies beyond.

steps.name: Male Instrument Shop Owner
steps.text: I brought a can of sand from the old beach here, too!

steps.name: Female Instrument Shop Owner
steps.text: If the volcano does end up erupting, the old place is going to be covered in ash, right?

steps.name: Female Instrument Shop Owner
steps.text: All the paths we've taken, the shops we visited, the beaches we walked... Everything will be buried under a pile of volcanic ash.

steps.name: Male Instrument Shop Owner
steps.text: But you'll still remember our party here tonight, won't you?

steps.name: Female Instrument Shop Owner
steps.text: Of course... This, too, is a new memory.
The shop owner strums the guitar, and the voices of the crowd romping around can be heard from afar.

steps.name: Cold Drinks Shop Owner
steps.text: Hey, you guys aren't gonna dance?

steps.name: Cold Drinks Shop Owner
steps.text: This is the time to dance, kids! If all you do is eat and chat, that's not a party!

steps.name: Male Instrument Shop Owner
steps.text: Here, let me play something!

steps.name: Male Instrument Shop Owner
steps.text: Care to join us, ma'am?

steps.name: Byrd
steps.text: Of course.
Byrd strums her guitar strings, and the gentle melody starts to envelope this city plate. Lying on the grass, the people gaze at the night sky, fireflies, and the stars up above.
Then, with a buzz, a disharmonic electric sound can be heard.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: Volcanic activity indicates Mount Siesta will very likely erupt within the next few hours.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: The nomadic city has already departed the area that will be affected by the eruption. There is no need for alarm.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: The tremors brought by eruption could lead to a tsunami. All citizens should evacuate coastal areas immediately. All citizens should evacuate coastal areas immediately.

steps.name: Passerby A
steps.text: It's happening? Today? Now? Really picked a terrible time.

steps.name: Passerby B
steps.text: Maybe it's the perfect time.

steps.name: Passerby A
steps.text: What do they mean by 'evacuate coastal areas immediately?' Is this place gonna be flooded? What about all this stuff? Are we taking anything with us? Anything we leave is gonna get washed away, right?

steps.name: Passerby B
steps.text: Don't take anything, just go!
The shop owner stops playing and looks at his partner. The oil fumes originating from the barbecue have yet to dissipate, and her face is still tinted red from the joy that has yet to fade.
She regretfully puts down her barbecue skewers.

steps.name: Female Instrument Shop Owner
steps.text: Hmm, it's possible that after we leave, the waves will swallow all our footprints today... including my grill and your guitar.

steps.name: Male Instrument Shop Owner
steps.text: Looks like the volcano and the sea are here to help us say goodbye to all that we had in our past.

steps.name: Male Instrument Shop Owner
steps.text: We should head upwards. It won't get flooded there. We'll have a new life.

steps.name: Female Instrument Shop Owner
steps.text: Over at the city center? I'm always worried that it could be too cramped there. There's not enough room for all your instruments and my grill.

steps.name: Male Instrument Shop Owner
steps.text: But there's enough room for the two of us.
The owner looks into his partner's eyes. His eyes are glittering.
Suddenly, she starts laughing.

steps.name: Female Instrument Shop Owner
steps.text: Right...! That's more than enough!

steps.name: Male Instrument Shop Owner
steps.text: That's right, dear. That's more than enough.

steps.name: Male Instrument Shop Owner
steps.text: Come! Let's get Tom, what with how old and frail he is. We can't just leave him here to cry over his precious ice cream.

steps.name: Female Instrument Shop Owner
steps.text: Hey—Tom—! Time to go! If we don't leave before the waves come, you'll get sucked into the sea with all your ice cream!

steps.name: Cold Drinks Shop Owner
steps.text: Ow... Oww...

steps.name: Cold Drinks Shop Owner
steps.text: Where's the young lady who helped me bring the ice cream? We can't leave her behind...

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: (Found it...)

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: (The two missing pages. There's no doubt that this is Professor Katia's handwriting. There's also the military's wax seal.)

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: (Keller, what exactly are you hiding...?)

steps.name: Worker
steps.text: Dr. Kahn?

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: It's you... Where's Professor Keller?

steps.name: Worker
steps.text: The signal from the volcano's monitoring station cut off two hours ago, and the data we got in the end was really strange.

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: Why didn't she inform anyone?

steps.name: Worker
steps.text: She said the situation was critical, and she had to inspect it herself.

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: Did she go alone?

steps.name: Worker
steps.text: No, the intern from Leithanien went with her, I think.

steps.name: Anxious Passerby
steps.text: We made it to the safety zone, right...?

steps.name: Nervous Passerby
steps.text: This place is over a hundred kilometers from the volcano. I'm sure we'll be fine...

steps.name: Nervous Passerby
steps.text: I mean, that's what city hall said...

steps.name: Anxious Passerby
steps.text: But... don't you feel the ground shaking?

steps.name: Harley
steps.text: Enis! Have you seen Liv?!

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Is she not home...?

steps.name: Harley
steps.text: She wasn't there when I got back. You mean she didn't go look for you?

steps.name: Enis
steps.text: Shit...

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: Huh? Everybody's gone... Did everyone go have fun somewhere else?

steps.name: Girl
steps.text: Are you the only one here...? Did you get left behind by your friends, too?
The transport is parked at the foot of the mountain. The once familiar mountain range now sports a completely different appearance.
The flora on the mountain has withered long ago, and the rugged rockscapes now look taller than ever.
With the sun gradually setting, a dark shadow is draped over the two researchers' minds.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: So this is Mount Siesta...

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: Adele, be careful.

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: This is as far as the transport will take us. We have to walk the rest of the way.

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: Monitoring Station No. 1 is halfway up the volcano. We still have a long walk ahead of us.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: I'm fine. My energy can keep up still.

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: Hmm...
The scholar lowers her head. her heart is rending with a sharp, piercing pain.
Just who is the terrified one?
The volcano is right in front of her, but she cannot bring herself to take a single step forward.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Professor Keller. Are you okay?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Would you like to take my hand?
Streams colored dark red can be seen slowly climbing their way through the mountain rocks like the blood veins in one's body, all while the enormous thing breathes strenuously.
From the earth's core to this cliff, they flowed through the ages, enduring an intense heat and utter silence.
This path seems to not be nearly as long as Adele had imagined. With the strength she has, she can still climb onto this mountain.
But this path also seems to be much longer than she had imagined. It's long enough for her memories to be rinsed countless of times at the bottom of her heart.

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: This is where we set up the monitoring station.

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: This equipment... Has someone been here?

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: But there are no other footprints on the mountain...

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: The Originium energy response hasn't changed, but the temperature measurement instruments logged a high response...
She takes a look around and can make out only the dark mountain gravel and molten rocks in the shadows.

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: How strange...

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: The event has most likely ended. Let's tune the instruments and head back.

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: Kahn, what are you doing here?

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: (Out of breath)

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: I heard... you two... climbed the volcano...

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: Why...?

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: Adele was worried because the monitoring station's indices were fluctuating, so we came here to inspect.

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: It was probably caused by accident. We're preparing to evacuate to a safe observation point.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: The volcanic activity is definitely starting to pick up. The eruption might happen sooner than expected...

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: Yeah, we need to go.

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: Stay right there, Keller.

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Kahn?
The man, still out of breath, is trembling. He pulls out a file from his chest, and the moment Keller sees its cover, her expression changes immediately.

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: September 1095, on Mount Unna, why did you suddenly leave the survey team...?

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: And in November that year, you didn't attend the Naumanns' funeral, but someone said they saw you at a symposium with the military at Wilhelm University.

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: On top of that, not even Adele has seen Katia Naumann's research data. What is it doing in a letter between you and the Leithanian military?!

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: Keller, answer me!

steps.name: Adele
steps.text: Professor Keller...?

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: Adele, I told you that I'd share everything with you when this observation is done...

steps.name: Keller
steps.text: Kahn, it's dangerous here. We should—

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: Keller... Look where we're standing. The Naumanns were here, on this very volcano.

steps.name: Kahn
steps.text: Are you still going to lie, even here?!

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: Hmm... I'm not really one to interfere with human affairs.

steps.name: Dolly
steps.text: But this isn't the place for a row...
